subject: Clarify marketplace invoicing: withholding & VAT evidence for cross-entity co-sell

Subject: Clarify marketplace invoicing: withholding & VAT evidence for cross-entity co-sell

Hi Lucy / ACME team,

Quick question as we approach contract signature for ACME: the purchasing entity is an EU-registered company (VAT ID provided), but ACME asked that the AWS marketplace invoice route the charge through their US reseller entity for marketplace co-sell. Two specific asks so we can hand to Finance:

1) For a US reseller (seller-of-record) invoice, what documentation does AWS/ACME expect from us to avoid backup withholding or to justify a zero-withholding treatment? (e.g., a completed W-8BEN-E tied to Redwood as the non-US payee, or will ACME's SOR status change the form required?)
2) For the EU customer, will AWS/ACME accept reverse-charge VAT evidence (VAT ID + invoice language) on your marketplace flow, or do we need to provide additional proof (signed declaration or local tax form)?

We want to ensure the invoice can be routed to ACME's US entity without creating VAT or withholding exposure for the customer or Redwood. If there's a standard DocuSign packet or SOR invoice template you can share, that would speed up Finance review.

I've attached a redacted sample W-8BEN-E and the customer's VAT docs to this thread for context.

Thanks — Camila

Subject: Re: Clarify marketplace invoicing: withholding & VAT evidence for cross-entity co-sell

Hi Camila — thanks for the clear summary. Short answers and what we need from each party: 

1) US reseller / SOR handling:
- If ACME is acting as seller-of-record in the marketplace, AWS will issue the invoice to ACME US entity. Backup withholding is generally not an AWS responsibility for charges settled to the SOR; however, to avoid Redwood being treated as a US payee for withholding, we typically request a W-8BEN-E from the actual service provider (Redwood) on file. That W-8BEN-E should be dated and reference Redwood's non-US status. ACME as SOR will have its own W-9 on file with AWS for US tax reporting.

2) EU VAT / reverse charge: 
- For EU buyers where the VAT reverse charge applies, AWS supports passing the VAT ID and reverse-charge notation on the invoice line item when the buyer's VAT ID is supplied at purchase time. We also sometimes require a copy of the buyer's VAT certificate or a screenshot from the national VIES lookup for validation — especially for cross-border B2B transactions. A signed declaration is not usually required unless local law or the buyer's tax advisor asks for it.

Requested artifacts to attach to the HubSpot deal and to send to AWS Billing team:
- Completed W-8BEN-E for Redwood (signed, PDF).
- ACME's W-9 (for SOR).
- Buyer VAT ID (VIES screenshot or certificate).
- Copy of the SOR agreement or marketplace co-sell memo showing that ACME will be invoiced.

I'll drop the SOR invoice template link here: https://www.docusign.com/link/sor-invoice-template — ACME can populate and route via DocuSign; once AWS Billing confirms SOR assignment we can route settlement to ACME and avoid Redwood getting US withholding.

Lucy Hall

lucy.hall@amazon.com

On a process note: we'll need Finance to confirm that the W-8BEN-E you supplied maps to Redwood's legal entity and tax ID. If you want, I can loop in our AWS billing contact to a call this week with ACME and Redwood Finance to close the evidence loop.
